# Classification models

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## Classifier

`protocol Classifier` — A protocol for supervised classification models that predict discrete class labels.

- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Int]` — Predicts class labels for the given feature vectors. Returns: An array of predicted class labels, one per sample.
- `func predict(_ value: Double) -> Int` — Predicts a single class label from one single-feature sample. Returns: The predicted class label.
- `func classify(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Classification]` — Groups input features by their predicted class label. Returns: An array of `Classification` groups, one per unique predicted label, sorted by label.

## LogisticRegression.Outcome

`enum Outcome` — The outcome of the descent run that produced this model. Mirrors `Outcome` — both objectives run the one shared loop, so they report convergence the same way. *(since 1.4.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Hashable.

- `init?(rawValue: String)` *(since 1.4.0)*
- `case converged` — The convergence test fired within the iteration cap. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `case maxIterationsReached` — The optimizer used every available iteration without satisfying the convergence test. The returned coefficients are the best-so-far estimate. Confirm meaningful descent by comparing `lossHistory`'s first and last entries before trusting the result. *(since 1.4.0)*

## LogisticRegression

`struct LogisticRegression` — A binary classifier trained by gradient descent on cross-entropy loss. *(since 1.4.0)*

Conforms to: Classifier, Codable, Equatable.

- `let coefficients: [Double]` — The fitted coefficient vector. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of features the model was trained on. Does not count the intercept term. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `let hasIntercept: Bool` — Whether this model includes an intercept (bias) term. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `let learningRate: Double` — The learning rate that was used during fitting. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `let iterations: Int` — Number of iterations the optimizer used before stopping. Equal to `lossHistory.count − 1` because the trajectory begins with the loss at the initial all-zeros parameters. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `let finalLoss: Double` — The final cross-entropy loss at the returned coefficients. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `let lossHistory: [Double]` — The full loss trajectory, beginning with the cross-entropy loss at θ = 0 and ending with `finalLoss`. Length is `iterations + 1`. Inspecting this array is the canonical way to see whether descent was smooth or stalled. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `let outcome: Outcome` — Whether the run converged or hit the iteration cap. See `Outcome`. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int], learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> LogisticRegression` — Fits a logistic regression classifier to the given training data. Returns: A trained `LogisticRegression` model. Throws: `divergedNonFinite(iteration:loss:)` when the iterate produces a `NaN` or `±∞` loss; `divergedIncreasing(iteration:previousLoss:currentLoss:)` when the loss strictly increases between iterations beyond the tolerance. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `static func fit(features: [Double], labels: [Int], learningRate: Double = 0.01, maxIterations: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1.0e-6, intercept: Bool = true) throws -> LogisticRegression` — Fits a logistic regression classifier from a single feature array. Returns: A trained `LogisticRegression` model with `featureCount` of 1. Throws: `GradientDescentError` on divergence. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Int]` — Predicts class labels for one or more samples. Returns: An array of predicted class labels (0 or 1), one per sample. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func predictProbabilities(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — Predicts the probability of class 1 for one or more samples. Returns: An array of class-1 probabilities, one per sample. *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func decisionFunction(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Double]` — Returns the raw linear score Xθ — the log-odds — for one or more samples. Returns: An array of log-odds scores, one per sample, each in (−∞, +∞). *(since 1.4.0)*
- `func decisionFunction(_ value: Double) -> Double` — Returns the log-odds score for a single-feature sample. Returns: The log-odds score Xθ for that sample. *(since 1.4.0)*

## KNearestNeighbors

`struct KNearestNeighbors` — A trained K-Nearest Neighbors classifier.

Conforms to: Classifier, Codable, Equatable.

- `let trainingFeatures: [[Double]]` — The training feature vectors, stored for distance computation at prediction time.
- `let trainingLabels: [Int]` — The training labels, one per feature vector.
- `let k: Int` — The number of neighbors to consider for each prediction.
- `let metric: DistanceMetric` — The distance metric used to compare samples.
- `let weight: VoteWeight` — The weighting strategy for neighbor votes.
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of features the model was trained on.
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int], k: Int = 3, metric: DistanceMetric = .euclidean, weight: VoteWeight = .uniform) -> KNearestNeighbors` — Fits a K-Nearest Neighbors model to the given training data. Returns: A trained `KNearestNeighbors` model.
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Int]` — Predicts class labels for one or more samples. Returns: An array of predicted class labels, one per sample.

## VoteWeight

`enum VoteWeight` — The weighting strategy for neighbor votes in K-Nearest Neighbors.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Hashable.

- `case uniform` — Each neighbor gets one vote regardless of distance.
- `case distance` — Closer neighbors get more influence: weight = 1 / distance.

## DistanceMetric

`enum DistanceMetric` — The distance metric used to compare two vectors.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `case euclidean` — Euclidean distance: √Σ(aᵢ − bᵢ)².
- `case cosine` — Cosine distance: 1 − cosine similarity.
- `case manhattan` — Manhattan distance: Σ|aᵢ − bᵢ|. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `case chebyshev` — Chebyshev distance: max|aᵢ − bᵢ|. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `case squaredEuclidean` — Squared Euclidean distance: Σ(aᵢ − bᵢ)². *(since 1.6.0)*
- `case minkowski(p: Double)` — Minkowski distance: (Σ|aᵢ − bᵢ|ᵖ)^(1/p). *(since 1.6.0)*

## GaussianNaiveBayes

`struct GaussianNaiveBayes` — A trained Gaussian Naive Bayes classifier.

Conforms to: Classifier, Codable, Equatable.

- `let classes: [ClassStats]` — The learned statistics for each class, one entry per unique label.
- `let featureCount: Int` — Number of features the model was trained on.
- `static func fit(features: [[Double]], labels: [Int]) -> GaussianNaiveBayes` — Fits a Gaussian Naive Bayes model to the given training data. Returns: A trained `GaussianNaiveBayes` model.
- `func predict(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [Int]` — Predicts class labels for one or more samples. Returns: An array of predicted class labels, one per sample.
- `func predictLogProbabilities(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [[Double]]` — Returns log-probabilities for each class for each sample. Returns: 2D array of log-probabilities, shape [samples × classes].
- `func predictProbabilities(_ features: [[Double]]) -> [[Double]]` — Returns calibrated class probabilities for each sample. Returns: 2D array of class probabilities, shape [samples × classes]. Each row sums to 1.0. *(since 1.1.0)*

## GaussianNaiveBayes.ClassStats

`struct ClassStats` — Statistics learned from the training data for a single class.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let label: Int` — The class label this entry represents.
- `let prior: Double` — Prior probability P(class), computed as count / totalSamples.
- `let means: [Double]` — Mean of each feature for samples in this class.
- `let variances: [Double]` — Variance of each feature for samples in this class.
- `let count: Int` — Number of training samples belonging to this class.

## Classification

`struct Classification` — A group of data points sharing the same predicted class label.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Sequence.

- `let label: Int` — The predicted class label for this group.
- `let points: [[Double]]` — The input data points assigned to this class.
- `var count: Int { get }` — The number of data points assigned to this class.
- `func makeIterator() -> IndexingIterator<[[Double]]>` — Returns an iterator over the data points in this classification group.

## Array extensions where Element == Int

- `func confusionMatrix(actual: [Int], positiveLabel: Int = 1) -> ConfusionMatrix` — Builds a confusion matrix comparing these predictions against actual labels. Returns: A `ConfusionMatrix` containing the four outcome counts and derived metrics.
- `func accuracy(actual: [Int], positiveLabel: Int = 1) -> Double` — Fraction of predictions that match the actual labels: (TP + TN) / total. Returns: The accuracy as a value between 0 and 1.
- `func precision(actual: [Int], positiveLabel: Int = 1) -> Double?` — Of all predicted positives, what fraction were correct: TP / (TP + FP). Returns: Precision as a value between 0 and 1, or `nil` if undefined.
- `func recall(actual: [Int], positiveLabel: Int = 1) -> Double?` — Of all actual positives, what fraction did the model catch: TP / (TP + FN). Returns: Recall as a value between 0 and 1, or `nil` if undefined.
- `func f1Score(actual: [Int], positiveLabel: Int = 1) -> Double?` — Harmonic mean of precision and recall: 2 * P * R / (P + R). Returns: F1 score as a value between 0 and 1, or `nil` if undefined.
- `func classificationReport(actual: [Int]) -> ClassificationReport` — Returns a formatted per-class classification report comparing these predictions against actual labels. Returns: A `ClassificationReport` with per-class metrics, accuracy, and macro/weighted averages.
- `func classDistribution() -> [Int : Int]` — Returns the number of samples per class as a dictionary. Returns: A dictionary mapping each unique label to its sample count. Returns an empty dictionary if the array is empty.
- `func imbalanceRatio() -> Double?` — Returns the ratio of the largest class to the smallest class. Returns: The ratio of the largest class count to the smallest, or `nil` if the array is empty or contains fewer than two classes.

## Array extensions where Element == Double

- `func rSquared(actual: [Double]) -> Double` — Coefficient of determination R² comparing these predicted values against actuals. Returns: R² as a value between 0 and 1 (can be negative for very poor models).
- `func meanSquaredError(actual: [Double]) -> Double` — Mean squared error comparing these predicted values against actuals. Returns: The mean squared error (always non-negative).
- `func rootMeanSquaredError(actual: [Double]) -> Double` — Root mean squared error comparing these predicted values against actuals. Returns: The root mean squared error (always non-negative).

## ConfusionMatrix

`struct ConfusionMatrix` — Captures the four outcomes of a binary classifier — true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives — and derives standard evaluation metrics from them.

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let truePositives: Int` — Positive samples the model correctly identified as positive.
- `let falsePositives: Int` — Negative samples the model incorrectly identified as positive.
- `let trueNegatives: Int` — Negative samples the model correctly identified as negative.
- `let falseNegatives: Int` — Positive samples the model incorrectly identified as negative.
- `var accuracy: Double { get }` — Fraction of all predictions that were correct: (TP + TN) / total.
- `var precision: Double? { get }` — Of all predicted positives, what fraction were actually positive: TP / (TP + FP).
- `var recall: Double? { get }` — Of all actual positives, what fraction did the model catch: TP / (TP + FN).
- `var f1Score: Double? { get }` — Harmonic mean of precision and recall: 2 * P * R / (P + R).

## ClassMetrics

`struct ClassMetrics` — Per-class metrics for a single class label in a classification report. *(since 1.2.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let label: Int` — The class label this row describes. For aggregate rows (macro/weighted average), this is set to the sentinel `-1` and callers should consult the aggregate accessors on `ClassificationReport` rather than reading `label`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let precision: Double?` — Precision for this class (TP / (TP + FP)). `nil` when the model made no positive predictions for this class. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let recall: Double?` — Recall for this class (TP / (TP + FN)). `nil` when there are no actual samples of this class in the ground truth. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let f1Score: Double?` — F1 score for this class — the harmonic mean of precision and recall. `nil` when either precision or recall is undefined. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let support: Int` — The number of actual samples of this class in the ground truth. For aggregate rows, this is the total sample count. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `init(label: Int, precision: Double?, recall: Double?, f1Score: Double?, support: Int)` *(since 1.2.0)*

## ClassificationReport

`struct ClassificationReport` — A frozen snapshot of a multi-class classification's evaluation metrics. *(since 1.2.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let perClass: [Int : ClassMetrics]` — Per-class metrics keyed by class label. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let classOrder: [Int]` — Class labels in sorted ascending order — the canonical iteration order. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let accuracy: Double` — Overall accuracy across all samples. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let macroAverage: ClassMetrics` — Unweighted mean of per-class metrics. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let weightedAverage: ClassMetrics` — Mean of per-class metrics weighted by support. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let totalSupport: Int` — Total number of samples across all classes. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `init(perClass: [Int : ClassMetrics], classOrder: [Int], accuracy: Double, macroAverage: ClassMetrics, weightedAverage: ClassMetrics, totalSupport: Int)` *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func markdownTable() -> String` — Renders the report as a Markdown table — one row per class, plus the aggregate rows. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func csvRows() -> String` — Renders the report as CSV with one row per class plus the aggregate rows. *(since 1.2.0)*
